groups.defect: test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op (line 15), so the newly added time.sleep(0.1) meant to let flusher threads process (line 62) does nothing and the test remains racy.

answer.reasoning: Both suggestions name the same root cause and symptom: the global time.sleep monkeypatch at line 15 turns the added time.sleep(0.1) wait at line 62 into a no-op, so test_basic races. They are in the same file and test function and differ only in where they anchor (the patch line vs the wait block). One fix covers both: stop patching the sleep used for synchronization, or wait on a condition. s_8fdca476's extra remark that the flusher's own sleep becomes a busy loop is another effect of the same patch, not a distinct defect. So this is not a partial overlap.
